title: Render-to-temp + copy breaks merge/splice on-conflict against the working tree
body: If a projection renders into a fresh temp dir and the rendered output is then copied into the working tree, any merge-with-existing semantics in the projecting code (merge-managed-key-only for JSON, preserve-outside-block for managed-block-inline) sees only the empty temp dir — the merge target is always blank — so the working tree's unrelated keys / outside-block content gets clobbered on the copy step. For real-write modes, project DIRECTLY into the working tree so the merge/splice code sees the existing state. For dry-run, clone the relevant subset of the working tree into a shadow temp dir first, project into the clone, then diff clone vs working tree. Bit us in the post-EXECUTE review of RFC-0001's distribution-adapters spec; the unit tests passed because they re-ran into the same output dir (which carried the prior render), but the integrated --self path broke silently.

title: shutil.copytree follows symlinks by default — supply-chain hazard for published artifacts
body: `shutil.copytree(src, dst)` defaults to `symlinks=False`, which means symlinks in `src` are DEREFERENCED — the link target's contents land in `dst`. Same for `shutil.copy2` (default `follow_symlinks=True`). When projecting source files that may be attacker-controlled (third-party packs, plugin submissions, untrusted catalogues) into a published output tree, a malicious symlink to `/etc/passwd` exfiltrates the build host's secrets into the artifact. Pass `symlinks=True` to copytree and `follow_symlinks=False` to copy2 — they preserve symlinks as symlinks rather than dereferencing. Caught by the security-reviewer pass on RFC-0001's distribution pipeline; not exploitable today (packs are repo-owned) but lethal the day production packs from PRs are admitted.

title: Document a JSON-Schema subset in spec + plan + validator docstring, all three in sync
body: A stdlib-only Python validator forces a documented subset (no $ref, no oneOf, etc.). The spec's AC needs to enumerate the subset; the plan's task Approach needs to enumerate it; the validator's module docstring needs to enumerate it. If any of the three drifts, a future agent extends one and not the others, and the next adversarial review surfaces it as a Blocker. Worth a single source of truth across docs + code from day one. Applies to any RFC where stdlib-only is a hard constraint and a subset of an external standard is the contract.

title: Rename audits must enumerate docstring + comment + error-message sites, not just code constants
body: When a rename touches a name-that-is-an-identifier (filename, directory, package), the per-task line-level audit in the plan must list every string-literal occurrence — including module docstrings, header comments, assertion messages, help strings, and CLI-arg examples — not just code constants. The brief's `grep` Done-when test surfaces every site; the plan's per-task list is what executes against it. If the plan enumerates only constants, docstrings drift past EXECUTE and the post-EXECUTE adversarial-reviewer raises them as Blockers. Caught on PR#22 (relocate adapter contract to docs/contracts/): the round-1 plan listed only `CONTRACT_PATH` / `SCHEMA_PATH` constants in T3/T4; round-2 post-EXECUTE review found 14 docstring + assertion-message hits the audit had missed. Fix: when the reference taxonomy says 'Class X always rewrites', the per-task audit's grep must cover docstrings, comments, and message strings in the same sweep.

title: TOML datetime round-trip injection: a bare-datetime field can come back as `str` and carry phantom payload on re-emit
body: When a TOML emitter writes `installed-at = 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z` (bare offset-datetime literal), `tomllib.loads` parses that as a Python `datetime`. If a *different* writer (adversarial, hand-edited, third-party) writes `installed-at = "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\nphantom = \"injected\""` (TOML basic-string position instead of bare datetime), `tomllib` parses the same key as a Python `str` containing a real newline and quote bytes. Bare re-emission `f"installed-at = {entry['installed-at']}"` then lands phantom TOML structure on the next round-trip — even though the first-write side is clean. The fix has two layers: (1) filter prior entries at read time, requiring `isinstance(value, datetime)` for any field that's spec'd as a bare datetime; drop or warn on mismatch. (2) Store new entries as `datetime` (not a strftime'd string) so the emit loop has one uniform type and always applies the canonical strftime itself. Bit us during round-3 adversarial review of the TOML-injection hardening PR; the pack-metadata side was already closed but the marker round-trip path was a separate vector. Generalises to any TOML field where the schema says 'bare type X' but the loader will accept 'basic-string containing arbitrary bytes' at the same key.

title: Bash-to-Python port: heredoc rc was normalised; naked `return violations` leaks the raw count
body: When bash invokes a Python heredoc as `python3 - args <<PY ... PY` and the heredoc ends with `sys.exit(1 if violations else 0)`, the heredoc's rc is captured by `$?` as exactly 0 or 1 — bash callers everywhere pattern-match on `rc -eq 1`. A naive port that hoists the heredoc body into a Python function returning `violations` (an int count) and `sys.exit(<count>)` at the top level silently widens the rc shape: with 2+ violations, rc=2; rc>125 is reserved territory. Callers like `tools/test-*.sh`'s `[[ $got -eq 1 ]]` or a CI `if rc == 1` branch silently miss the failure. Aggregators that only check non-zero (like our `pre-pr.py`) mask this further. The fix is one line: `return 1 if violations else 0` at every exit site. Bit us in the post-EXECUTE review of windows-hooks-phase3; lint-build.py's two return paths both leaked the count. Generalises to any bash-heredoc-to-Python-function port — the parity-pinning bar is the rc *shape*, not just "non-zero on failure".

title: Bash-to-Python port: `"foo" in path.parts` matches segment at *any* depth where bash `-not -path './foo/*'` was top-level-anchored
body: Bash `find . -not -path './node_modules/*' -not -path './.git/*'` is anchored at the leading `./` — only TOP-level `node_modules` or `.git` are excluded. The Python equivalent `if "node_modules" in path.parts` excludes a `node_modules` segment at ANY depth, so a nested `packages/x/node_modules/y/AGENTS.md` is silently skipped where bash would still apply the per-package lint. The divergence is invisible until someone adds a nested vendor dir, at which point lint coverage shrinks without warning. The fix: `if path.parts[:1] in (("node_modules",), (".git",))` — anchor to position 0. Surfaced in the post-EXECUTE adversarial review of windows-hooks-phase3's lint-agents-md.py port. The general rule for path-glob transliteration: read the bash glob as anchored (`./X/*` = top-level) or unanchored (`*/X/*` = any depth) and pick the Python predicate that matches the anchor, not the substring.

title: Cross-surface parity (lint vs drift gate): `bytes.strip()` and `str.strip()` are not equivalent — Unicode whitespace creates a silent acceptance gap
body: When two checking surfaces claim parity over the same shape — e.g. `lint-agents-md.py` accepting both real symlinks and a one-line file containing `"AGENTS.md"` for the repo-root CLAUDE.md alias, and `self_host.py`'s drift detector being asked to match — the natural Python idioms `bytes.strip()` and `str.strip()` differ in what counts as whitespace. `bytes.strip()` only strips ASCII whitespace (`\t \n \r \v \f` + space); `str.strip()` strips Unicode whitespace too (NBSP U+00A0, IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE, etc.). A `CLAUDE.md` containing `"\xc2\xa0AGENTS.md\xc2\xa0"` (NBSP-padded) passes a `read_text(...).strip() == "AGENTS.md"` lint but fails a `disk_bytes.strip() == b"AGENTS.md"` gate. The realistic window is narrow (no Windows checkout produces NBSP padding) but the docstring/spec claim 'mirrors check #2's strip() semantics' becomes a lie unless the gate decodes first: `disk_bytes.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip() == "AGENTS.md"`. Surfaced in round-2 adversarial review of AC15b (PR #77). General rule: when two surfaces claim parity, test both the acceptance side AND the rejection-boundary side, and pick predicates from the same domain (both bytes or both str) — not the convenient mix.

title: Don't wire any lint into the projected pre-pr.py; a lint CAN ship to adopters as a skill script
body: Never wire a lint into tools/hooks/pre-pr.py: it's PROJECTED to adopters (sourced from packs/core/.apm/hooks/pre-pr.py), so it would call a script absent from their tree. That principle stands. But the corollary 'linters don't project, so they must be catalogue-only in tools/' is FALSE (RFC-0016 originally claimed it; corrected in RFC-0016 § Errata + ADR-0007). A skill's scripts/ folder DOES project to every adapter and already ships governance Python (work-loop/scripts/loop-cohort.py, new-adr/new-rfc scripts/next-ordinal.py). The doc-drift spec-metadata lint now lives at packs/core/.apm/skills/work-loop/scripts/lint-spec-status.py — agent-invoked at the work-loop finish-time checklist (available, not fail-closed), AND run by the catalogue as a fail-closed CI gate via `make build-check` against the PROJECTED .claude/ copy (mirrors how pre-pr.py invokes projected loop-cohort.py). Also: adding a file under packs/core/seeds/ changes the `core` install snapshot — regenerate with UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 pytest tests/integration/test_install_snapshot.py.

title: Prose-path-extraction lints: gate on full rooted paths, exclude placeholder/glob/brace shorthand, pair each exclusion test with an accepting control
body: When a lint extracts file paths from prose (e.g. the spec-metadata lint's invariant (iii) flagging dangling code references in specs), false positives are the dominant risk. Three rules keep it precise: (1) only treat a token as a path if it's a FULL repo-relative path — contains '/', rooted at a known top-level dir (packages/ tools/ packs/ docs/ apps/ .github/) or an explicit ../ / ./ relative link, ending in a recognised extension after stripping a :line/#anchor locator; bare basenames (install.py) can't be located and must be skipped. (2) Exclude non-literal shorthands: placeholders (<...>), globs (*), AND brace-expansion ({a,b}.py) — all denote not-a-single-path. (3) In the self-test, PAIR each exclusion case with a shape-matched ACCEPTING control that DOES fire (e.g. glob `tools/lint-*.py` rejected + `tools/lint-missing.py` warns), so a no-op extractor that matches nothing fails the suite instead of passing every reject vacuously. Keep such a check WARN-ONLY until the corpus warn rate is measured — promoting to hard requires the existing backlog of true positives (often on Frozen specs you can't edit) to be cleaned first. Dogfooding catch: the lint will flag its OWN spec's illustrative example paths — use real resolvable paths (e.g. the lint's own path under packs/core/.apm/skills/work-loop/scripts/) as examples, not tools/x.py.

title: No gate resolves relative Markdown links — a directory move leaves silent 404s for months
body: build-check does not resolve relative links in Markdown, and lint-spec-status.py's dangling-reference check is warn-only and covers docs/specs/ alone. So a relocation ADR (ADR-0055 lifting docs/contracts/ and docs/guides/ to repo root) leaves every `](../contracts/...)` and `](../guides/...)` in docs/architecture/ pointing at a deleted directory, and nothing fails. When a doc change touches paths at all, resolve every relative link in the touched files against the actual tree — `(file.parent / target).resolve().exists()` — before claiming the links are fixed. A grep proving the string changed proves only that the string changed. Two related traps in the same pass: (1) links can break by *removal* rather than depth (tools/run-pack-evals.py and tools/lint-agent-artifacts.py were folded into CLI subcommands at v0.13.0), so the resolver finds both classes but they need different fixes; (2) a systemic wrong-depth pattern repeated across a whole tree may be correct in the projected location that tree ships to — check before sweeping.

title: Starlight renders headings display:inline inside .sl-heading-wrapper
body: Starlight (0.41) wraps every markdown heading in <div class="sl-heading-wrapper level-hN"> and sets the heading itself to display:inline (for anchor-link hover). Any block-level decoration — border-bottom rules, full-width padding — applied to the h2 selector renders at text width, not column width. Put block decoration on the wrapper (.sl-heading-wrapper.level-h2) and keep type styles on the heading. Caught by visual QA in the docs-site-design-refresh; the short hairline under h2s was invisible to build gates.

title: Verify remark plugins fire by grepping built output — wrong registration fails silently
body: Astro accepts and silently ignores a malformed markdown config: `markdown: unified({ remarkPlugins: [...] })` type-checked and built green while the plugin never ran, so mermaid fences reached Expressive Code as plain code blocks and no placeholder div was ever emitted. The correct form is `markdown: { remarkPlugins: [...] }`. A transform's absence is invisible to build exit codes — after wiring any remark/rehype plugin, grep the built HTML for the transform's artifact (e.g. data-mermaid) before trusting it. Bit us for an unknown number of releases: the docs site's diagram pipeline had never actually worked.

title: plan.md is byte-pinned from approve-plan until the run's final cohort verb
body: loop-cohort's canonical plan hash normalizes whitespace only, so ANY plan.md content edit after `approve-plan`/`schedule` — including flipping the Status line to Executing — breaks the wave-guard hash and stops `wave-complete`. Sequence discipline: (1) `schedule` requires tasks as `### T<n>` headings, so convert the task list BEFORE the approval pair; (2) do not touch plan.md between approve-plan and the final `review record`; (3) flip plan Status to Done only at finish, after the last cohort verb. Recovery from a broken baseline: cohort-only reset + re-init with the same run-id (engine history survives).

title: Fontsource variable packages: default index.css is wght-only
body: For a Fontsource variable font, the package's default `index.css` export registers only the wght axis. Optical sizing (opsz) — and other axes — live in separate stylesheets (e.g. `@fontsource-variable/source-serif-4/opsz.css`). Wiring the bare package name into Starlight customCss silently drops optical sizing: the family renders, font-variation-settings 'opsz' does nothing, and nothing fails. Import the axis-carrying stylesheet explicitly and verify the axis appears in the built @font-face rules.

title: Per-file subprocess loops in test harnesses scale with spawn cost, not file size
body: A shell loop that spawns a process per file (`for f in ...; do mkdir -p ...; cp -P ...; done`) looks cheap and is not: cost is spawns x per-spawn latency, and per-spawn latency is a property of the machine, not the repo. Measure it before optimising anything else — `time (for i in $(seq 1 1000); do /bin/echo -n; done)`. Dev machines running endpoint security have measured ~26ms per spawn here vs ~1ms on CI Linux, which is why a harness can take 30 min locally and 112s in CI. Rewriting one such loop (2 spawns x 3,100 files x 6 seedings) as a single stdlib-Python pass cut tools/test-pre-pr.sh from ~28-37 min to ~4-8 min. Two behaviours the shell gave implicitly must be re-added by hand: `cp -P` overwrites an existing destination but shutil.copy2(follow_symlinks=False) raises FileExistsError (unlink first), and a read loop handles arbitrary path bytes but bytes.decode() aborts on non-UTF-8 (use os.fsdecode). Also check whether `set -e` is actually in effect at the call site before relying on it to catch the new command's exit.

title: A partly-generated content directory hides two traps: a projected file reverts, a gitignored one absorbs the edit
body: web/src/content/journeys/ is part hand-maintained, part generated: tools/build-site.py regenerates 11 of the 17 files from packs/<pack>/JOURNEY.md. A fix applied only to the web/ copy survives until the next build-site.py run, then silently reverts. Before editing any file under a directory a generator writes into, check whether that specific file has an upstream source; the directory being partly hand-maintained is not evidence that the file you are editing is. Second trap, same directory: one generated file (journeys/product-documentation.md) is listed in a local .gitignore, so `git status` counted 37 changed files when 38 values were edited, and no git-status-based check can ever observe it reverting - assert its content directly. Reconcile the count of values you intended to change against git status and explain any gap before believing a sweep is complete. Caveat on attribution: do NOT assume a revert was caused by the projection just because a projection exists. When the same docsUrl fix was undone (PR#852 -> PR#854), the projection explained at most 11 of the 37 reverted files - the other 26 are never generated - and a stale base was disproved outright (git merge-base --is-ancestor showed #852 already in #854's ancestry). Verify the mechanism against the commit graph before writing it down; a plausible mechanism that is present is not the mechanism that fired.

title: 'git commit -a' commits conflict markers; 'git stash' and plain 'git commit' refuse
body: On an unmerged (UU) path the three obvious escapes behave differently: 'git stash' fails with '<file>: needs merge', plain 'git commit' refuses with 'Committing is not possible because you have unmerged files', but 'git commit -a' SUCCEEDS — its implicit 'git add -u' marks the conflict resolved and commits the file with '<<<<<<<' intact. Any tooling or guidance that offers commit as the safe alternative to stash must special-case the unmerged branch, or it hands the agent a one-step path to committing conflict markers. Verified on git 2.50.1.

title: Classifying a git failure by its message needs LC_ALL=C
body: git's die()/error() strings are gettext msgids wrapped in _(), so a build with translation catalogues installed prints them in the user's language. A script that branches on 'couldn't find remote ref' (or any other English wording) silently stops firing on such a machine — and the fallback branch is usually the generic one, so it fails quietly rather than loudly. Set LC_ALL=C in the subprocess env before matching. GNU gettext ignores LANGUAGE when the locale is C, so LC_ALL alone is enough. Apple Git ships no catalogues, so this is invisible on macOS.

title: A pack version bump is three files; build-self syncs none of them
body: 'FORCE=1 make build-self' projects pack CONTENT into .claude/ and .agents/, but it does not propagate a pack's version. Bumping packs/<pack>/pack.toml alone leaves packs/<pack>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json and the root .claude-plugin/marketplace.json stale, and 'make build-check' passes anyway — the catalogue verifier's CAT-V-005 check looks at pack_dir/plugin.json rather than pack_dir/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, so it silently no-ops. The agentbundle pytest suite is what catches it. Bump all three by hand in the same commit.

title: A coverage linter that reads Makefile variable assignments is permanently green
body: When a gate asks "is this CI target also run locally?", build the local set from invocation positions only — recipe lines of the targets your entrypoint transitively reaches, and the argv of the scripts it spawns. Never scan the whole file for path-shaped tokens: `SAST_DIRS := tools packs packages` yields `tools`/`packs`/`packages`, which are directory prefixes of nearly every path in the repo, so prefix-based coverage marks everything covered and the gate reports clean forever. Over-extraction on the CI side is the safe direction (a spurious target forces a human to write an exemption); over-broad coverage on the local side is fatal and silent. Pin it with a self-test asserting those bare tokens are absent from the extracted set.

title: Reporting a missing test-manifest entry as a failing test
body: A runner that iterates a list of (label, argv) and counts non-zero exits will report an entry whose file does not exist as "2 of 9 failed" — a sentence about tests that ran. Validate every entry's target before running anything and exit with a distinct code (0 pass / 1 a test failed / 2 the manifest is broken). Treat an entry from which no target path can be extracted as a manifest error too, or a bare `-m pytest` preflights clean while verifying nothing. Two entries sat red for weeks here because the message read like ordinary test failure.

title: git stash is shared across worktrees — never park work with it when agents run in parallel
body: `refs/stash` lives in the common git dir, so every linked worktree (git worktree, Conductor workspace, any parallel-agent setup on one clone) pushes to and pops from the same stack. A concurrent rebase elsewhere will pop your stash into its tree, and your pop will land its untracked files in yours — which then fail your repo's own linters for reasons that look unrelated. Park work with a local commit (`git commit`, later `git reset --soft HEAD~1`) instead; commits are per-worktree. Recovery: `git log --all --format='%H %s' | grep <marker>` (not `git fsck --unreachable`, too slow on a large repo); a stash commit has three parents, and the untracked files are in the third.

title: A test that shells out with os.environ inherits CI's variables and passes only locally
body: When a case asserts behaviour that branches on an environment variable, build the child's env explicitly and CLEAR the keys under test — `env={**os.environ, **extra}` inherits whatever CI sets. A case asserting the not-in-CI branch then takes the in-CI branch on the runner and fails there while passing on every laptop. Seen with GITHUB_WORKFLOW: the case set only SKIP_SAST, inherited the runner's real GITHUB_WORKFLOW, and took the wrong branch. Pin the scrub with one case that sets the variables ambient and asserts the declared branch still wins.

title: A lint that reads runner call sites will parse the comment that documents the rule
body: Prose explaining a constraint naturally quotes the exact command it forbids — a Makefile comment saying "do NOT collapse these into `pytest packs/*/tests/`" contains that invocation. A line-based parser over Makefiles, workflows and Python sees it as a real call site, so the explanation of the rule violates the rule. Skip lines whose stripped form starts with the file's comment marker before matching. Every one of 92 failures on the first corrected run of tools/lint-pack-test-boundary.py was a comment.

title: `grep -c` in a CI floor assertion silences the case the floor exists for
body: `n=$(cmd | grep -c '::')` exits 1 when nothing matches, so under GitHub Actions' `bash -e` the assignment aborts the step before the `::error::` line runs. A partial loss prints a diagnostic; a total loss — the exact case a minimum-collected floor exists to catch — reds with no message at all. Append `|| true` to the substitution.

title: A local `npm install` under packs/ slows every test that builds a catalogue
body: `package.py`'s `packs/**` archive walk applies no deny-list, and agentbundle's own tests copy `packs/` into temp dirs and build. One `npm install` in a skill with a package.json adds ~10k gitignored files there, and the suite slowed by more than an order of magnitude — with zero signal, because node_modules/ is gitignored so nothing in review or `git status` shows it. Remove it after any local JS verification.

title: `## Acceptance criteria` is silently ungated — lint-spec-status matches case-sensitively
body: lint-spec-status.py collects checklist items with `^##\s+Acceptance Criteria\b` and no re.IGNORECASE, so a spec whose heading reads `criteria` collects zero and invariant (ii) — every AC checked or deferred at the ship transition — passes vacuously forever. Eight specs in this repo are in that state and three more carry no criteria heading at all. Copy the heading from packs/core/.apm/skills/new-spec/assets/spec.md rather than typing it.

title: Guarding the collision that announces itself instead of the one that is silent
body: When two skill test dirs are collected by one pytest process, duplicate *test* basenames make pytest error out loudly — easy to diagnose, not worth a lint. The failure worth guarding is the duplicate *subject* module: a sys.path sibling import binds one skill's render.py for both suites and everything passes green. Check both, and say which was found. Exclude conftest.py from the test-basename comparison — one per directory is pytest's design, so counting it reports every multi-directory invocation as a collision for a reason that is false.

title: Coverage recorded only in a spec note freezes when the spec ships
body: "Which suites actually run" written into docs/specs/<feature>/notes/ is accurate on the day it ships and never again — shipped specs are frozen, so the next test directory is unrun by default with nothing saying so. Encode it instead as a lint case: enumerate the destination directories, require each to be named by a runner call site or listed in an in-source exemption set with a one-line reason, and fail on a stale exemption whose directory is gone.

title: A gate is not a gate until you have watched it reject something
body: Adding a schema, a validator call, or a test is not the same as adding a gate. Five distinct instances in one change, each of which reported green while checking nothing: (1) contracts/plugin-manifest.derived.schema.json described a plugin `source` object, but build/main.py pops `source` before validate_derived_plugin_manifest_dict, so it never saw one — proven by every live marketplace entry carrying `category`, which that schema forbids; (2) a new verify.py check placed the root-marketplace validation below an `if not dist_dir.exists(): return []` early return, making it unreachable in CI, where dist/ is gitignored and never built; (3) both schemas loaded in one try/except that returned [] on failure, so one missing file silently disabled the entire step — including the check that already worked; (4) a spec specified `oneOf` for a constraint, but build/validate.py lists oneOf/anyOf/allOf as 'Unsupported by design', so the real gate ignores it while a jsonschema-based test goes green; (5) test stubs used `pytest.importorskip('jsonschema')`, absent from pyproject dependencies=[] and from CI, turning four assertions into silent skips that pass locally. The cheap discriminator is a negative probe: feed the gate something it MUST reject and assert a non-empty diagnostic list. Every one of these was caught that way and none by a passing suite. Corollary: `<gate> | tail -n` and `<gate>; echo $?` after a pipe report the FILTER's exit code, not the gate's — run gates unfiltered and read the real exit code.

title: An SCA gate resolves requirement pins against the public index, so a pin cannot lead its release
body: `pip-audit -r <requirements.txt>` (and npm/cargo equivalents) resolves every pin against the public registry, not the workspace. In a monorepo that both publishes a package and pins it from a consumer, raising the consumer's floor to the version this PR bumps to makes the SCA leg fail with 'Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement' until that version is actually published. It is a merge-ordering constraint, not a code defect, and it cannot be closed from inside the PR. Decide it up front: publish first, or land the pin in a follow-up and let the runtime feature-detect carry the floor. Do NOT carve the file out of the scanner — that removes coverage from exactly the dependency you just changed. Surfaced when credbroker 0.5.0's floor landed in the same PR as the bump.

title: A platform-skipped assertion inside a cross-platform parity suite reads as coverage and proves nothing
body: Adding a test suite to a Windows/macOS parity runner only exercises what its assertions actually run. A test guarded by `skipif(os.name != 'posix')` skips on the very runner it was added for, so the platform-specific arm stays unverified while a green run is read as verifying it — worse than no test, because it retires the 'named limitation' caveat without earning it. Write the assertion cross-platform where you can (spawn a grandchild via subprocess.Popen rather than os.fork; probe liveness via os.kill(pid, 0) on POSIX and tasklist on Windows), or state in the AC that the arm remains unverified.

title: One large socket read is unbounded in wall-clock even with a socket timeout
body: A socket timeout applies per `recv`, not per `read()`. So `fp.read(cap + 1)` against a server that sends one byte at a time resets the clock on every byte, and the read is bounded only by cap x timeout — 64 KiB at 5 s is hours. Any deadline you enforce *before* the request does not constrain the body read at all. Read in chunks and re-check the deadline between them. Matters most on a credential or auth path, where the fetch target can be attacker-influenced (e.g. a URL taken from a WWW-Authenticate header) and the caller is a synchronous operator command that simply hangs.

title: A check whose green state coincides with the feature being broken
body: Before specifying a verification check, ask which states make it pass. Two instances found in one session: a static assertion that every <pre class="mermaid"> carries an aria-label passed only because the client-side bundle replaces that <pre> when it succeeds, so the attribute survives exactly when rendering fails; and a goal-based `grep -n '^| D46' decisions.md` passed while a blank line above the row had silently terminated the markdown table, so the row rendered as literal pipe text. Both tested an artifact one step upstream of the thing that matters. Confirm the check goes red in the failure it exists to catch, not just green when things are fine; where the property only exists at runtime, the check has to run there.

title: A blank line silently ends a markdown table, and a row-presence grep still passes
body: Appending a row to a markdown table that is followed by a blank line puts the new row *after* the blank, which terminates the table -- the row renders as literal pipe-delimited text. It happened twice in one change (D46, then D47). A `grep '^| D46'` Done-when check passes either way because the bytes are present. Assert adjacency to the previous row instead, or parse the table.

title: attr_list attribute values are not escape-safe, and the sink may not be HTML
body: python-markdown's attr_list does not escape values: a value containing a double quote terminates the attribute and the remainder becomes markup -- a compiler-emitted label of 'Diagram & "3.1" <script>x</script>' put a live <script> into the published page. A single HTML-escape closes that completely and round-trips the value exactly, including ampersands, em dashes, accents and CJK, so an ASCII allowlist is the wrong control and destroys international text for nothing. But check the value's real sink before choosing the control: where a theme lifts the attribute into Mermaid source as accTitle:, '%%{init:...}%%' is consumed as a Mermaid *directive* and an embedded newline destroys the diagram, so those need rejecting at emission. Escape for the HTML hop, reject for the second hop.

title: Prove a process makes no network request with kill-on-egress, and run the negative control first
body: To show a subprocess never reaches the network, blocking egress and checking the exit code only proves it tolerates failure. On macOS use sandbox-exec with '(deny network-outbound (with send-signal SIGKILL))' so any attempt is fatal: completion then proves no attempt from any code path, including compiled extensions a Python-level socket tracer cannot see. Validate the instrument before trusting it -- trivial process survives, IP-literal connect is killed (a DNS-only block lets hardcoded IPs through), DNS-based urlopen is killed, the same request succeeds unsandboxed. '(with report)' is rejected on a deny action and sandbox denials did not reach the unified log on Darwin 25.5, so log scraping is not a substitute. Does not port to Linux CI: use a network namespace or seccomp filter, with its own negative control.

title: Resolve and preflight installed skill entry points before interpreting exit codes
body: Agents run commands from the session's project root, not the installed skill directory. A skill must obtain the installer-supplied directory containing its active SKILL.md, canonicalize the skill-owned scripts directory and expected entry point, require a resolved regular file confined beneath that directory, and only then launch it as one argv element while retaining the project root for content paths. Missing, non-file, resolution-error, or escaping targets stop before runtime launch with a bounded installation or invocation diagnostic. This ordering matters because CPython exits 2 when it cannot open a script, colliding with the user-action band used by credentialed clients and Mermaid Renderer; Node exits 1 with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. No in-process guard can disambiguate an interpreter that never started the script. Shell-string-only adapters must use a platform-safe literal form or refuse the path. Apply the same renderer to every command the skill teaches or emits, including dependency setup and eval expectations, and test the production command builder's exact argv rather than quote counts or an isolated helper.

title: A test that moves with the code cannot catch the code being wrong
body: Asserting set equality between a projection's output and the same module's own eligibility flag is tautological: when the flag is wrong, both sides move together and the test stays green. Mutation-test any guard you add — delete the branch and confirm a named test fails. If nothing fails, the test documents the implementation rather than constraining it. Pin invariants against an independent expectation (a literal set, a frozen fixture) rather than against another output of the code under test.

title: grep -E with an escaped pipe matches a literal, so a negated guard always passes
body: Under `grep -E`, `\|` is a literal pipe character, not alternation. A check written `! grep -qE "x('\|/)" file` matches nothing, so the negation succeeds unconditionally and the guard can never fail. Always pre-verify an absence check against the pre-change file: it must exit non-zero *before* the change, or it is proving nothing.

title: Collate source material into a declared inventory before projecting it
body: When generating an artifact from a source tree, split the work into a collate pass that emits one record per file with every awkward fact as a declared field, and a projection pass that consumes those records. Each exception (files that must not surface, path normalizations, override fields) becomes a visible field rather than a branch buried in projection logic, the before/after diff is computable so 'nothing regressed' is proven rather than asserted, and the two halves are testable independently.

title: A house-style rule put in the shipped package becomes an adopter's build break
body: `pack.schema.json` and `agentbundle.build.lint_packs` both ship inside the published package and run against third-party catalogues via `agentbundle validate` and `agentbundle catalogue lint`. Adding an editorial rule (a prose-length cap, a wording convention) to either one silently exports this repository's taste as a hard failure in someone else's build. Repo-only policy lints belong in `tools/` as a `lint-x.py` + `test-lint-x.py` pair, wired into BOTH `tools/repo/build_gate_chain.py` and `.github/workflows/build-check.yml` — `lint-ci-parity` fails if the two disagree, and it also needs a `STEP_DISPOSITION` entry naming the local target. The catalogue-curation guard (RFC-0059 D6) is what catches the mistake, but only after the fact: it refuses any changeset touching `packages/agentbundle/**` or `packs/credential-brokers/**` without an `Engine-Change-RFC:` trailer. Treat that refusal as a design signal, not an obstacle to route around with the trailer.

title: make build-check runs the gate chain; it cannot detect a step missing from the chain's own pinned list
body: `tools/test_build_gate_chain.py` pins the exact `build-check` step sequence in `EXPECTED_SCRIPT_STEPS`. Adding a step to `tools/repo/build_gate_chain.py` makes `make build-check` run it and pass, while Gate F (`pytest tools/test_build_gate_chain.py`) fails — the local gate exercises the chain, the CI gate asserts its shape. A green `make build-check` says nothing about that list. Adding a gate step means editing three places: the chain, `EXPECTED_SCRIPT_STEPS`, and `build-check.yml` plus its `STEP_DISPOSITION` entry in `tools/lint-ci-parity.py`.

title: Editing a scaffold-projected guide requires a package-data resync AND the curation-guard trailer
body: Several `guides/_shared/**` files are projected into `packages/agentbundle/_data/catalogue-scaffold/`. Editing one drifts the scaffold; `make build-check` misses it and `tests/integration/test_scaffold_projection.py` catches it. The fix is `python3 tools/catalogue/sync_authoring_scaffold.py --write` — but its output lands in `packages/agentbundle/**`, which the catalogue-curation guard protects, so the commit then needs an `Engine-Change-RFC:` trailer. That trailer accepts `n/a — <reason>` for a non-engine change; precedent is in #872 and #880. Do not invent an RFC number, and do not route around the guard.

title: A monorepo editable install resolves to one workspace for the whole machine
body: pip install -e packages/<pkg> records one absolute path, so with several Conductor workspaces on the same repo the global interpreter resolves that package from whichever workspace installed it last. Local gates then exercise a different checkout and pass or fail for reasons unrelated to your diff; when that workspace is deleted the import fails outright mid-session. Re-running the editable install just re-points the trap. Install into the workspace's own gitignored .venv instead and drive every local gate through .venv/bin/python, leaving the global interpreter on PyPI builds. Detect editables via pip list (shows a path) or dist-info/direct_url.json carrying dir_info.editable true.

title: Hashing an artifact your own workflow mandates editing breaks by construction
body: Before pinning a file with a content hash, list every write the surrounding workflow *requires* after the pin is taken. A lifecycle field the process itself bumps (a status token, a progress checkbox, a generated timestamp) will invalidate the pin one mandated step later, and the failure looks like tampering rather than a design error. Hash a canonical form that normalizes exactly the fields the workflow writes, and nothing else. Two traps when implementing it: substitute the token by a span-bounded splice, not str.replace, because the token usually recurs in a trailing vocabulary comment on the same line; and check whether any test already encodes the broken behaviour as intended, because those tests go green-to-red and read as regressions.

title: pytest.mark.parametrize list items evaluated at collection time
body: Bare attribute accesses like [errno.EOPNOTSUPP, errno.ENOSYS] inside a @pytest.mark.parametrize list are evaluated when pytest collects the module, not when the test runs. An AttributeError silently fails the *entire module*'s collection. Mirror any production-code getattr guard (e.g. _LOCK_UNSUPPORTED_ERRNOS) with an equivalent list comprehension at the module level instead.

title: A test directory named `build` is invisible to pytest and ruff
body: Both pytest default norecursedirs and typical ruff excludes carry the bare name "build". A suite at tests/build/ is skipped on recursion — `pytest tests/` reports green having collected none of it — and naming the directory as an explicit argument does not rescue it; only naming individual files does. It also never gets linted. Measured on one move: 587 tests and 73 lint violations silently absent. Name it something else (tests/build_pipeline/). The same bare name in a ruff exclude also hides a package genuinely named build/ from every repo-root run.

title: A test that supplies the wiring it is meant to verify
body: When a call site passes a config argument, a test that calls the same function and supplies that argument itself proves only that the function honours it — it survives the call site being deleted. Prove the difference by mutation: remove the wiring and confirm the test reddens. Caught three times in one change, each time one call site further out, and each time the test read as thorough. The general form is asserting your own intent rather than the system behaviour; drive the real entry point instead.

title: In-repository TMPDIR changes Git fixture semantics
body:
A TemporaryDirectory created beneath a checkout is still inside that checkout: git -C walks upward and may resolve the
    parent repository. Tests for no-repository or no-base behavior should initialize an explicit nested repository boundary without the
    ref, or place the fixture outside every checkout.
